1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif face at a comfortable size with visibly loose line spacing (e.g. the multi-line banner and log text), though no explicitly dyslexia-specific typeface or letter-spacing adjustment is evident.

2.why: Every screen uses short sentences, sentence case, bold only for labels/headings, and no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs.

3.why: Content is laid out in a single narrow centred column with full-width stacked buttons and inputs, which reads well at phone width, although the screenshots are rendered in a desktop viewport rather than an actual mobile size.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Get a six-digit identity code for this demo.' and 'Enter your identity code' are one short line of plain language.

5.why: Placeholders show expected formats ('name@example.com', '123456'), and demo credentials are displayed, though the password field has no example.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than one or two short sentences before acting; the longest text is the two-line activity-log explanation which is optional.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears anywhere; the demo email and password must be transcribed by hand and no secret is presented in a copyable form.

8.why: No QR code or scan-based alternative appears in any of the five screens; the flow never reaches authenticator setup.

9.why: Standard labelled email/password and numeric code inputs are used, which browsers may autofill, but nothing observable (autocomplete hints, one-time-code affordance, or password-manager prompt) confirms support, and on-screen demo credentials imply manual typing.

10.why: Each screen has a large emoji-paired heading and a single filled blue primary button, plus a four-segment progress bar, though the progress segments are unlabelled so the step number is not stated in words.

11.why: Steps 1 and 2 ask for one action only; step 3 shows 'Check code' alongside a secondary 'Re-request identity code', but the visual hierarchy makes the single primary action clear.

12.why: Green confirmation banners state outcome and next step explicitly ('Signed in successfully. Next: get your identity code.', 'Your identity code was requested. Next: enter the six digits.'), reinforced by the activity log.

13.why: The code screen allows unlimited retries and offers a 'Re-request identity code' button with no lockout or penalty shown, but no reveal/hide toggle for any secret is present.

14.why: The error reads 'That code does not match. Check the six digits, or request a new code.' — it names the problem and the fix without blaming the user.

15.why: Step 2 explicitly states 'There is no reading timer. Take as long as you need.' and no countdown, expiry timer, or auto-updating element appears on any screen.
